coverage: Candidate text for the currently identified calculator surfaces. Final wording, placement, and inclusion follow the open product decisions; this catalog does not approve new behavior.

quick.expression.placeholder.meaning: Invites the user to enter a mathematical expression.
quick.expression.placeholder.context: Shown only while the quick input is empty.
quick.expression.placeholder.location: Inside the centered quick calculation input.

quick.expression.accessibleName.meaning: Names the mathematical input for assistive technology.
quick.expression.accessibleName.context: Read when the quick input receives focus, including when a value is present.
quick.expression.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of the quick input; not an extra visible label.

quick.result.label.meaning: Identifies the value produced by the current expression.
quick.result.label.context: Used only when a valid result for the current expression is available. The result line is empty for unfinished input, and an earlier result must not stand in for the current one. Decimal formatting and reduced opacity of trailing digits are handled separately from this label.
quick.result.label.location: Result line directly below the quick input.

result.boolean.true.meaning: Displays a logical result whose value is true.
result.boolean.true.context: Used when the current valid calculation produces a logical value, such as 5 > 3. This is display text; accepted input literals remain separate. Quick result copy preserves the displayed localized text.
result.boolean.true.location: The active calculation result, directly below quick input or in the result area associated with an expression in a calculation sheet.

result.boolean.false.meaning: Displays a logical result whose value is false.
result.boolean.false.context: Used when the current valid calculation produces a logical value, such as 5 < 3. This is a valid result, not an error or a missing result. Accepted input literals remain separate. Quick result copy preserves the displayed localized text.
result.boolean.false.location: The active calculation result, directly below quick input or in the result area associated with an expression in a calculation sheet.

completion.list.accessibleName.meaning: Names the list of suggested expression completions for assistive technology.
completion.list.accessibleName.context: Used when suggestions open from the first letter in quick or multiline input, or immediately after a complete :: or to conversion operator. Up to seven rows are visible; arrow selection scrolls to keep the active option visible. While open, Up and Down select, Tab accepts, and Escape closes only the suggestions. Compatible target units are suggested after a conversion operator; comments do not open suggestions. Search ordering is still being specified.
completion.list.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of the suggestion list aligned beneath the currently typed word. One frame surrounds the list, which overlays following text without shifting it and may cross the input area's lower boundary. A visible heading is not required.

completion.showDescription.meaning: Opens the complete description of the selected suggestion when the inline text is shortened.
completion.showDescription.context: Available for a selected suggestion with a description. The complete text must be accessible by keyboard as well as pointer hover; the exact shortcut and presentation are still being specified. User-authored descriptions remain in their original language.
completion.showDescription.location: Command or keyboard help associated with the selected suggestion. The exact control placement belongs to the full interface prototype.

completion.function.sin.description.text: Sine. Enter the angle in degrees.
completion.function.sin.description.meaning: Explains that the ordinary sine call takes its unmarked numeric argument in degrees.
completion.function.sin.description.context: Shown when the sine function is suggested. Ordinary input such as sin(30) uses degrees without a suffix; explicitly marked radian input such as sin(pi/2 rad) is also supported. Both behaviors were reconfirmed in expression-language round 15. The typed matching prefix is visually reduced in opacity; the proposed continuation is fully opaque.
completion.function.sin.description.location: Immediately after the complete sine signature in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. The description uses the same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, with no shared-column or right-edge alignment.

completion.function.sqrt.description.text: Square root of a nonnegative number.
completion.function.sqrt.description.meaning: Explains the square root function within the calculator's real-number domain.
completion.function.sqrt.description.context: Description shown when the square root function is suggested. Negative real arguments are outside the accepted numeric domain. The typed matching prefix is visually reduced in opacity; the proposed continuation is fully opaque.
completion.function.sqrt.description.location: Immediately after the complete square-root signature in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. The description uses the same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, with no shared-column or right-edge alignment.

completion.unit.squareMetre.description.meaning: Identifies a square metre as a unit of area.
completion.unit.squareMetre.description.context: Shown when this area or volume unit is offered as a completion. Tab inserts the displayed superscript unit symbol. Contextual-units round 8 extends shorthand 2/3 formatting to every known length symbol, including explicit length aliases, but only to whole symbols; a longer name prefix must not be rewritten. Backspace deletes the exponent and formatting adds no separate undo step. m2/m3 never denote minutes. A caret raises a whole quantity and is not an equivalent completion spelling. Pasted formula text follows the same formatting and has one undo for the entire paste; selected formula text is copied with visible ²/³ characters. Numeric result copy omits the unit and its superscript but preserves displayed numeric rounding in quick mode, history and sheets. See the context-specific copy help for targeting and focus.
completion.unit.squareMetre.description.location: Immediately after the unit spelling in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. Same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, without column or right-edge alignment.

completion.unit.squareCentimetre.descrip.location: Immediately after the unit spelling in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. Same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, without column or right-edge alignment.

quick.history.show.context: With the completion menu closed, Up Arrow in quick mode expands history and immediately recalls the preceding saved formula into the fixed input; repeated Up presses recall older formulas while the list moves downward through the console. Preserve the original input and cursor/selection from before browsing so Down can return to it. An open completion menu retains its existing arrow-key priority. The proposed separate Tab history mode was not accepted. Expanded-mode opening uses a separate Alt+Up command accepted in copying round 16; see help.history.extendedShortcutRule.
quick.history.show.location: Command menu or keyboard hint associated with quick input.

quick.history.hide.meaning: Collapses history while retaining the quick input.
quick.history.hide.context: Available when history is expanded. Round 17 accepts automatic collapse when Down Arrow returns to the original input, whether empty or nonempty, restoring its cursor/selection. Further Down at the original input does not erase it. Up stops at the oldest saved entry. Successful ordinary Enter confirmation also collapses history. These quick-mode boundaries do not change the separate search or expanded-sheet history contexts.
quick.history.hide.location: Command menu or keyboard hint associated with expanded history.

quick.sheet.open.meaning: Switches to a calculation with variables and multiple expressions.
quick.sheet.open.context: Used by a separate mode-entry command with a modifier; its exact shortcut is undecided. A new sheet starts with the current expression at the same screen position and expands downward. A previously hidden sheet remains available without losing its contents.

quick.hide.meaning: Dismisses the visible calculator without naming a full application exit.
quick.hide.context: Used by Escape when suggestions are closed, the repeated summon shortcut, or a click on another application. If suggestions are open, the first Escape closes only the suggestions. The unfinished input is preserved when the calculator hides.
quick.hide.location: Command menu or keyboard help; not standard window chrome.

definitions.saveConstant.meaning: Publishes a user-defined named formula for reuse, retaining its dependencies on other saved constants.
definitions.saveConstant.context: Explicit publication under round 18. A draft does not change the working definition before Save. Correct publication recalculates current quick input and open dependent sheets; invalid syntax, unknown references or forbidden cycles preserve the working version and the editable draft. Assigning or autosaving a local sheet variable does not publish it globally. New definitions must not silently overwrite an existing global name. The header comment description is published with the definition. Exact action access and storage-failure handling remain separate design work.
definitions.saveConstant.location: Definition actions associated with the calculation editor; the exact menu placement is not yet specified.

definitions.saveFunction.meaning: Saves a user-defined calculation rule for future calls by name.
definitions.saveFunction.context: Explicit publication under round 18 for short or multiline functions with sequential local intermediates and a final result expression. Parameters and own locals resolve alongside saved global definitions, without implicit caller-sheet capture. Invalid syntax, unknown references, recursion or cycles preserve the working version and draft. Validation is not a guarantee of success for every numerical argument. Header descriptions publish with the definition. Current dependent calculations recalculate; saved history answers do not. Exact action access and storage-failure handling remain separate design work.
definitions.saveFunction.location: Definition actions associated with the calculation editor; the exact menu placement is not yet specified.

copy.result.meaning: Copies the targeted valid calculation result.
copy.result.context: Accepted through copying round 2: Ctrl+C on Windows / Cmd+C on macOS in the editor with no text selection copies the single ready displayed result entry, even if that entry groups several interpretations. Click copy targets the clicked entry. Numeric result copy omits the unit: 4m copies 4, and 5m/s copies 5. Preserve displayed numeric rounding, all shown digits, signs, numeral-system prefix/case and grouping; do not copy hidden precision or change working values. Formula selection copies the selected visible text, including units. If multiple displayed entries exist while the editor has focus and no text is selected, the shortcut leaves the clipboard unchanged and shows copy.chooseResult. Count all entries after display grouping, including horizontal overflow. Quick copy keeps the window, formula and cursor, restores input focus after a click and creates no history. Missing or stale results of the current input cannot be copied. Round 15 accepts clicking a displayed history answer to copy its saved displayed value without recalculation. Changes to constants or functions do not make that historical answer ineligible; use the saved answer that was clicked, not the currently calculated value or the answer chosen at confirmation. Preserve the current formula and cursor, return focus to input and leave the stored record and confirmation choice unchanged. The same numeric-only and localized logical payload rules apply. Keyboard selection for confirmation was accepted in round 6. Round 14 accepts Ctrl+C/Cmd+C while focus is in the current result row: copy the highlighted ready answer and keep selection and focus there. An inactive text selection retained in the editor does not change this target. The editor copy shortcut retains its accepted behavior. Enter confirmation is a separate accepted action: in quick mode with one ready displayed result, it records history and copies with the same payload rules, then starts empty input while keeping the window open. Enter never accepts a completion suggestion. Round 17 accepts keyboard copy in history opened from an expanded sheet: Up/Down choose a record, Left/Right choose a saved answer and Ctrl+C/Cmd+C copies that answer with the same payload, preserving the sheet and history focus. This is not copying a freshly evaluated sheet expression or recalling its formula; Enter separately inserts the formula.
copy.result.location: Copy action for quick-mode results, clicked saved history answers, and the selected saved answer in history opened from an expanded sheet. Copy targets for freshly calculated sheet expressions remain to be specified.

copy.success.meaning: Confirms that the clipboard write succeeded.
copy.success.context: Feedback only after a result has actually been written to the clipboard successfully. Ctrl+C/Cmd+C and click quick copy preserve input and add no history. Full quick-mode confirmation success also requires saving history: Enter then starts empty input in the open window, while Ctrl+Enter on Windows / Cmd+Enter on macOS hides the window with empty input on the next invocation. This message confirms only the clipboard write and must not imply that a failed history write succeeded or that selected formula text was copied as a result. A confirmation failure preserves the formula, result and open window. Successful Enter also collapses expanded history; failure does not. Retrying an incomplete confirmation without changing the formula, calculation or chosen answer must not duplicate an already saved history entry; after full success, apply the command used for the retry. Operation order and recovery after restart remain architecture decisions. Exact feedback presentation remains open. For quick copy with focus in the current result row, keep focus and selection on the highlighted answer; this feedback must not move focus back to the editor. Clicking a current answer still returns focus to input. Round 15 accepts click-copy of a saved historical answer, preserving the current formula and cursor and returning focus to input. Report success for the saved displayed value actually copied, without recalculating it or changing history. For accepted round-17 clipboard copy in expanded-sheet history, the success feedback must preserve history focus and the unchanged sheet; it does not imply formula insertion or a new history record.
copy.success.location: Brief copy feedback associated with the input/result region and its accessible live region. Presentation when confirmation resets input or hides the window is to be verified.

copy.error.text: Could not copy the result. Try again.
copy.error.meaning: Reports that writing the result to the clipboard failed.
copy.error.context: Shown or announced only when writing a result to the clipboard fails, including shortcut/click quick copy and the copy step of Enter or modified-Enter confirmation. A failed quick-mode confirmation preserves the formula, result and open window and shows this brief error; it must not clear input or hide the window. Do not use this message for a history-save failure or claim success. Retrying an incomplete confirmation without changing the formula, calculation or chosen answer must not duplicate an already saved history entry; after full success, apply the command used for the retry. Operation order and recovery after restart remain architecture decisions. Failed confirmation also preserves the expanded history state. Copying a formula selection is a separate operation. Result-row shortcut copy uses the highlighted current answer; it does not fall back to copying an inactive editor selection. Quick copy does not confirm a calculation. This feedback also covers clipboard failure after clicking a saved history answer. Do not recalculate the historical expression or substitute a current answer as a fallback; do not claim a successful copy.
copy.error.location: Feedback area near the active result.

expression.invalid.meaning: Reports an expression that cannot be parsed.
expression.invalid.context: Shown for a syntax error after the agreed validation trigger.
expression.invalid.location: Diagnostic area associated with the current expression.

expression.divisionByZero.meaning: Explains why division cannot produce a result.
expression.divisionByZero.context: Shown when the current expression attempts division by zero during evaluation. The expression has no copyable result. An unselected conditional branch is not evaluated and must not trigger this message.
expression.divisionByZero.location: Diagnostic area for the affected expression or sheet line.

expression.unknownName.meaning: Reports an identifier that the calculation cannot resolve.
expression.unknownName.context: Shown when an expression refers to an undefined name.
expression.unknownName.location: Diagnostic area for the affected expression or sheet line.

placeholders.name: An identifier exactly as written by the user in the calculation. Preserve its spelling and do not translate the inserted value.

expression.domainError.text: This operation is not defined for these values
expression.domainError.meaning: Reports values outside the supported mathematical domain.
expression.domainError.context: Shown when a supported operation cannot accept the supplied values.
expression.domainError.location: Diagnostic area for the affected expression or sheet line.

expression.incompatibleUnits.meaning: Reports a conversion between incompatible measurement dimensions.
expression.incompatibleUnits.context: Shown when the requested unit conversion is invalid.
expression.incompatibleUnits.location: Diagnostic area associated with the conversion expression.

expression.unknownUnit.meaning: Reports a measurement unit that the calculator does not recognize.
expression.unknownUnit.context: Shown when a conversion uses an unsupported unit token.
expression.unknownUnit.location: Diagnostic area associated with the conversion expression.

placeholders.unit: A unit token exactly as written in the expression. Preserve the token; accepted unit spellings are defined by the expression language.

expression.precisionLimit.meaning: Explains that an entered number exceeds the supported numeric precision.
expression.precisionLimit.context: Shown for decimal input exceeding the supported 30-significant-digit precision. The input must not be silently truncated. Integer magnitude is checked independently of the number of written digits in the selected base and uses the dedicated integer-limit diagnostic. Exact rounding at the working-precision boundary remains under discussion.
expression.precisionLimit.location: Diagnostic area for the affected expression or sheet line.

expression.limit.text: This calculation exceeds the supported limits
expression.limit.meaning: Explains that evaluation stopped at a configured computational limit.
expression.limit.context: Shown when an expression is rejected for exceeding the supported complexity or evaluation budget. Long-running calculation mode is excluded; exact resource thresholds remain to be specified.
expression.limit.location: Diagnostic area for the affected calculation.

history.title.meaning: Names the list of past calculations.
history.title.context: Shown when the history view is expanded. Successful Enter confirmation in quick mode with one ready displayed result adds the calculation to history, copies its result, starts empty input and collapses expanded history. Arrow Up opens it again with the newest calculation nearest to the stationary input. Failed confirmation does not collapse history. The history expansion state on the next invocation after modified-Enter hiding is not yet selected. Copying round 7 fixes historical results at confirmation; changed constants or functions do not recalculate them. Recalling a formula into input calculates a new result with current definitions while preserving the original record.
history.title.location: Heading of the history region above the stationary quick input. Initially the newest entry is closest to the input; Arrow Up shifts the list downward into the console and Arrow Down shifts it upward.

history.empty.context: Shown when history contains no saved entries.

history.search.placeholder.meaning: Invites a search among past calculations.
history.search.placeholder.context: Search was accepted in copying round 9. Ctrl+F on Windows / Cmd+F on macOS in active quick mode opens history search over saved formulas and results. Preserve the current formula and its cursor and do not move its input field. Searching must not recalculate historical records. Copying round 10 accepts filtering as the query is typed. Up/Down choose a matching record without replacing the formula. Enter closes search and recalls the chosen formula for recalculation only, without copying, confirmation or new history. Escape restores the original formula and cursor. With no matches, Enter recalls nothing. Copying round 11 accepts case-insensitive substring matching in the formula or any saved displayed result. Matches retain the normal history order; an empty query shows the entire history. This does not change case-sensitive expression semantics or recalculate saved values. Copying round 12 accepts decimal point/comma and numeric digit-grouping equivalents, plus plain/superscript 2/3 in recognized length-unit area/volume spellings in the Latin baseline and active locale. Preserve ordinary substring matches and stored text. Do not normalize caret exponentiation into unit shorthand, rewrite names/comments, evaluate formulas or convert units/bases. See help.history.searchNotationRule. Exact field placement remains open.
history.search.placeholder.location: Search input inside the history region.

history.search.accessibleName.context: Read when the history search input receives focus. The accepted quick-mode search targets saved formulas and historical results, not the live recalculation. Search focus must preserve the formula draft and cursor for later return. Copying round 10 accepts filtering as the query is typed. Up/Down choose a matching record without replacing the formula. Enter closes search and recalls the chosen formula for recalculation only, without copying, confirmation or new history. Escape restores the original formula and cursor. With no matches, Enter recalls nothing. Copying round 11 accepts case-insensitive substring matching in the formula or any saved displayed result. Matches retain the normal history order; an empty query shows the entire history. This does not change case-sensitive expression semantics or recalculate saved values. Copying round 12 accepts decimal point/comma and numeric digit-grouping equivalents, plus plain/superscript 2/3 in recognized length-unit area/volume spellings in the Latin baseline and active locale. Preserve ordinary substring matches and stored text. Do not normalize caret exponentiation into unit shorthand, rewrite names/comments, evaluate formulas or convert units/bases. See help.history.searchNotationRule. Exact field placement remains open.
history.search.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of the history search input.

history.noMatches.meaning: Explains why a nonempty history search displays no entries.
history.noMatches.context: Shown when a nonempty search query has no matching saved formula or displayed result. Matching is case-insensitive substring search, updated as the query is typed; Enter recalls nothing without a match. Empty query shows all history in normal order; history.empty describes the state with no saved records. Search does not recalculate records or search only currently loaded rows. Copying round 12 accepts decimal point/comma and numeric digit-grouping equivalents, plus plain/superscript 2/3 in recognized length-unit area/volume spellings in the Latin baseline and active locale. Preserve ordinary substring matches and stored text. Do not normalize caret exponentiation into unit shorthand, rewrite names/comments, evaluate formulas or convert units/bases. See help.history.searchNotationRule. A record may still match its saved displayed result independently of its formula spelling.

history.entry.accessibleName.meaning: Proposes announcing a historical formula and its complete displayed set of saved results.
history.entry.accessibleName.context: Editorial accessible-name draft for a focused history entry. Copying rounds 7 and 8 accept storing the complete result set and showing the formula with all saved displayed answers in one horizontal row. The answer chosen at confirmation is bold when several answers exist; use the separate history.result.chosen description to make that distinction available without relying on font weight alone. Do not add visible interpretation captions, drop saved displayed alternatives or substitute the live recalculation. Exact list announcement and native accessibility behavior require prototype verification.
history.entry.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of a calculation history entry.

placeholders.expression: The historical mathematical formula, formatted for the active locale according to the existing unit-language rules. Do not translate or alter inserted user names or comments.
placeholders.results: The complete formatted set of saved displayed results for this history entry, including unit and numeral-system notation. Do not use the live recalculation or only the copied numeric value. List formatting and selection announcement are handled by the accessibility presentation and remain to be verified.

history.reuse.meaning: Returns the targeted historical formula to input for recalculation.
history.reuse.context: Used for a selected history entry. Accepted in copying round 7: the recalled formula is calculated anew with current user constants and functions; the original history record and its saved results remain unchanged. Navigation that recalls the formula does not itself confirm or create a new record. Successful confirmation records the new calculation under the existing Enter or modified-Enter flow. Retrying an incomplete confirmation with unchanged formula and calculation does not duplicate an already saved entry; copying round 8 accepts a separate record for every new successful confirmation, even when formula and results match an earlier record. Copying round 13 places this action in the shared history menu. A specific history entry is required; without one the action is unavailable. Invoking it recalls a copy for recalculation rather than confirming or copying its result.
history.reuse.location: Item in the shared history menu opened by right-clicking a history record or the quick-mode history-menu shortcut.

history.delete.context: Accepted in copying round 9: an explicit history action deletes one particular record without a confirmation dialog and provides history.undo. Identical records from separate confirmations are distinct targets. Constants, functions, sheets and templates are preserved. This does not bind Delete in the formula editor to record deletion. Copying round 10 accepts undoing deletions in reverse order until the application fully exits, including whole-history clearing as one operation. Hiding and reopening the window preserve Undo. Restore full removed records in their former order without removing calculations added later. Undo from the previous session is unavailable after a full exit. This is separate from formula text undo. Copying round 13 places this action in the shared history menu. It requires a specific target entry and is unavailable without one. Opening the menu is not invocation of deletion. Failure behavior and exact disabled presentation remain open.
history.delete.location: Item in the shared history menu, targeting one specific history record.

history.clear.context: Accepted in copying round 9: starts a separate confirmation before clearing the complete calculation history. Opening this action is not consent to deletion. Constants, functions, sheets and templates are preserved. Copying round 10 accepts undoing deletions in reverse order until the application fully exits, including whole-history clearing as one operation. Hiding and reopening the window preserve Undo. Restore full removed records in their former order without removing calculations added later. Undo from the previous session is unavailable after a full exit. This is separate from formula text undo. Copying round 13 includes this action in the shared history menu; a selected individual history entry is not required. Opening the menu does not start clearing.

history.clear.title.meaning: Asks the user to confirm clearing the calculation history.
history.clear.title.context: Confirmation flow accepted in copying round 9; exact wording is editorial. Shown before clearing the complete calculation history, never for deleting one record. Copying round 10 accepts undoing a full clear as one operation until the application fully exits; hiding the window does not end Undo availability.
history.clear.title.location: Title of the history clearing dialog.

sheet.title.meaning: Names a multi-expression calculation with variables.
sheet.title.context: Used as the generic extended-mode heading.
sheet.title.location: Heading of the extended calculation view.

sheet.name.label.meaning: Labels the user-defined name of a calculation sheet.
sheet.name.label.context: Shown when creating or renaming a saved sheet.
sheet.name.label.location: Label next to the sheet name field.

sheet.name.placeholder.meaning: Invites a name for a calculation sheet.
sheet.name.placeholder.context: Shown while a sheet name field is empty.

sheet.editor.accessibleName.meaning: Names the editor for variables and expressions.
sheet.editor.accessibleName.context: Read when the extended editor receives focus.
sheet.editor.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of the sheet editor.

sheet.new.context: Accepted in round 19: create a separate locally autosaved sheet through the shared library. Closing another sheet does not delete it; this command does not publish global definition drafts. Exact navigation focus and unsaved-storage-error behavior still need design.
sheet.new.location: Actions for the relevant sheet or template in the shared library or its opened document; exact menu placement remains interface work.

sheet.save.meaning: Saves the current sheet as a reusable local calculation.
sheet.save.context: Unassigned candidate label. Named sheets now autosave under round 17, point 6; the accepted flow does not require a manual Save sheet button. Do not treat this catalog entry as approval of an extra control or as permission to autosave global definitions.

sheet.rename.meaning: Changes the saved name of a sheet.
sheet.rename.context: Available for a named calculation sheet.
sheet.rename.location: Actions for the relevant sheet or template in the shared library or its opened document; exact menu placement remains interface work.

sheet.duplicate.meaning: Creates a separate copy of a calculation sheet.
sheet.duplicate.context: Accepted in round 19: creates a sheet with its own text, without modifying the source. Global definition references retain their existing live meaning.
sheet.duplicate.location: Actions for the relevant sheet or template in the shared library or its opened document; exact menu placement remains interface work.

sheet.delete.context: Accepted in round 19: delete this sheet without an extra confirmation dialog, with separate document deletion Undo until full application exit. Hiding keeps Undo. Other documents, history and global definitions remain; restoration must not overwrite newer data. The missing-global-dependency case is a pending round-20 proposal.
sheet.delete.location: Actions for the relevant sheet or template in the shared library or its opened document; exact menu placement remains interface work.

sheet.saveAsTemplate.meaning: Creates a reusable calculation template from a sheet.
sheet.saveAsTemplate.context: Accepted in round 19: save a copy of the sheet as a template, choosing local variables as parameters with default values. Template launch creates an independent named autosaved sheet; edits to that sheet do not change the template. Explicit template updates do not rewrite existing sheets. Detailed parameter-entry behavior remains a round-20 proposal.
sheet.saveAsTemplate.location: Actions for the relevant sheet or template in the shared library or its opened document; exact menu placement remains interface work.

sheet.saved.meaning: Confirms that the sheet was persisted successfully.
sheet.saved.context: Shown or announced only after a sheet has actually been persisted successfully, including the autosave accepted in round 17, point 6. Text may be incomplete or contain calculation errors and still be saved. This feedback does not confirm a calculation, add a history entry or save a global definition. Exact quiet status presentation and timing remain interface decisions.

sheet.saveError.meaning: Reports failure to persist the calculation sheet.
sheet.saveError.context: Reports failure of a sheet persistence attempt, including accepted automatic saving. A calculation error is not a save failure: incomplete and erroneous sheet text is still eligible for autosave. Do not claim successful persistence or apply this message to saving a global definition. Exact retry, recovery and feedback presentation remain separate work.

sheet.cycle.text: These expressions depend on each other
sheet.cycle.meaning: Explains a circular dependency that prevents automatic recalculation.
sheet.cycle.context: Accepted in round 17, point 3: sheet-local definitions may reference later definitions and are evaluated by dependency. A cycle blocks its participating definitions and downstream dependents; independent expressions still calculate. Use this diagnostic for actual cycle participants; use sheet.dependencyError for a downstream expression that is blocked but not itself in the cycle. Exact highlighting and accessible presentation require interface verification. This is the sheet model and does not introduce forward references or reactive evaluation into sequential user-function bodies.
sheet.cycle.location: Diagnostics for the affected sheet expressions.

templates.title.context: Names the template group of the shared library accepted in round 19. This does not require a second standalone template browser.
templates.title.location: Group heading for templates in the shared library.

templates.empty.context: Shown when no templates have been saved.

templates.search.placeholder.meaning: Invites a search by template name.

help.precedence.unitPowersRule.text: A final 2 or 3 on a complete known length-unit symbol automatically displays as a superscript: cm2 becomes cm², мм3 becomes мм³, ft2 becomes ft² and metre2 becomes metre². The same rule applies to explicit length aliases and to the Latin baseline plus one active locale. m2/m3 and м2/м3 always mean square/cubic metres, never minutes. Do not format a prefix of a longer name: m20 and m2rate remain unchanged; continuing the word removes the superscript formatting. Backspace immediately after m² deletes only the exponent, leaving m. Undo restores the preceding user input without an extra step for automatic formatting. Pasted formula text receives the same formatting as typed text: 2cm2 + 3cm2 displays as 2cm² + 3cm². One undo restores the state before the entire paste. Copying selected formula text puts the visible text on the clipboard, including actual ²/³ characters. Quick numeric result copy omits the unit and its superscript: 4m² copies 4. Displayed numeric rounding is preserved and the working value is unchanged. The caret ^ raises the entire quantity to a power: 2m2 denotes two square metres; 2m^2 leaves the supported answer 4m², discarding the squared-minutes interpretation. Unit support is checked after final cancellation. Shorthand autoformatting is not extended to time, mass or other dimensions.

help.precedence.unitPowersRule.context: Accepted through contextual-units round 9. Known length symbols include explicit metre/метр aliases and follow Latin-plus-one-active-locale availability. Formatting is based on a complete unit symbol, not a substring replacement inside an arbitrary name. The display rule does not approve the semantic parsing of m20 or choose a storage format. Round 9 approves identical formatting for pasted formula text, one undo for the entire paste and visible superscript characters when copying selected formula text. Backspace deletes the exponent and formatting adds no separate undo step. The metre/minute ambiguity is absent from square/cube unit shorthand. Copying round 2 omits units and their superscripts from quick numeric result copy while preserving displayed numeric formatting and working precision. Selected formula text still includes units and superscripts. Other copy commands, editing boundaries, stored-name conflicts and branch-error policies remain open.

help.precedence.durationNotation.text: Short duration symbols are w, d, h, m, s and ms. Russian symbols are н, д, ч, м, с and мс. Days remain 24 hours and weeks remain seven days. Adjacent duration components add, with or without spaces: 1h30m and 1h 30m both equal 90 minutes. Components may appear in any order and repeat: 30m1h equals 90 minutes; 1h30m15m equals 105 minutes. Use an explicit * to multiply adjacent duration quantities. With only ambiguous m symbols, retain both valid readings: 1m30m and 1m 30m give 31 minutes as a duration sum and 30 square metres as a length product. This does not introduce addition of adjacent lengths. A compound duration is one value for surrounding operators: 1h30m * 2 equals 180 minutes, and -1h30m equals minus 90 minutes. An incomplete final component such as 1h30 keeps the result blank until its unit is entered. An explicit operator is required before a following quantity of a clearly different dimension: 1h30m2km reports a missing operator; write 1h30m / 2km to calculate pace. This boundary does not remove the two accepted readings of 1m30m or other accepted forms of implicit multiplication.
help.precedence.durationNotation.meaning: Explains duration sums, accepted ambiguous readings, treatment as one value under surrounding operators, incomplete input and the boundary before another dimension.
help.precedence.durationNotation.context: Accepted through contextual-units round 7. Keep both operation readings and their values until whole-expression constraints are applied; do not force an ambiguous sequence to mean only duration. Examples describe value and dimension, not a new result notation or result caption. Original input is not automatically reordered. The explicit multiplication requirement applies to adjacent duration quantities, not to a duration followed by a parenthesized scalar expression. An unfinished 1h30 must not retain a stale answer or become multiplication by 30. A following quantity of a clearly different dimension requires an explicit operator. These duration rules do not regroup the separate length-product interpretation. Other token boundaries remain open.
