Identical full formatted answers, including units, appear once; interpretation captions remain excluded. Horizontal overflow does not reduce the entry count for copy eligibility. While the formula editor has focus, one ready displayed entry allows shortcut copy without text selection; multiple entries without text selection leave the clipboard unchanged and prompt the user to choose. A click targets an entry. Numeric result copy omits its unit while preserving displayed numeric formatting; dropping units for copying does not merge display entries or discard hidden meanings. In quick mode, Enter or modified-Enter with multiple answers first focuses this row and highlights the first entry without copying or recording. Left/Right navigate and reveal the focused entry through horizontal scrolling; a later confirmation command acts on that entry. Escape restores the formula cursor. A click remains copy-only and returns focus to input. These commands were accepted in copying round 6. Round 14 adds Ctrl+C/Cmd+C while this row has focus: copy the highlighted ready answer and keep focus and selection there, regardless of an inactive editor text selection. Typing, paste, Backspace and Delete end selection and perform the usual edit at the restored formula cursor/selection with live recalculation and no copy or confirmation. Round 15 accepts Left/Right stopping at row boundaries without wrapping, and Up/Down ending selection and immediately performing ordinary history navigation without copying or confirming. Round 16 fixes ordering for the known metre/minute ambiguity: metre before minute, ambiguous occurrences left to right; filtering preserves relative order and a grouped display stays at the first constituent position. Numeric magnitude and UI language do not reorder these answers. Other ambiguity kinds need an explicit ordering rule if included later. Other remaining keys, exact focus styling and screen-reader announcements still need decisions or prototype verification.
result.alternatives.label.location: Single horizontal scrollable result row beneath the fixed input, containing values and unit symbols without interpretation captions.

error.unsupportedUnit.meaning: Explains that no valid answer with a supported final unit remains.
error.unsupportedUnit.context: Accepted in contextual-units round 4. Final unit support is checked after cancellation; only interpretations with unsupported final units are discarded. Policies for other mathematical errors remain open. Use the accepted result ordering for known metre/minute ambiguity and the separate accepted copy/confirmation contracts; ordering for any later added ambiguity must be specified explicitly. Supported compound families are speed, pace and information-transfer rate; area and volume remain supported. Examples of excluded final units are kg*m, s² and m/s². Diagnostic precedence when other errors also occur is still undecided.
error.unsupportedUnit.location: Calculation diagnostic region when no valid supported-unit answer remains after final cancellation and interpretation filtering.

help.precedence.simpleCompoundUnits.text: Supported compound units are speed (length/time, for example km/h), pace (time/length, min/km) and information-transfer rate (information/time, MB/s). Area and volume remain supported. Check support after final cancellation: (2s * 3s) / 1s = 6s is valid. Final units such as kg*m, s² and m/s² are excluded. Discard interpretations with unsupported final units and show the remaining valid answers; show the short unsupported-unit diagnostic only if no valid supported answer remains. Policies for other errors are still being specified. Temperature retains its separate conversion-only rule.
help.precedence.simpleCompoundUnits.meaning: Defines the limited supported compound-unit families while retaining area and volume.
help.precedence.simpleCompoundUnits.context: Accepted in contextual-units round 4. Final unit support is checked after cancellation; only interpretations with unsupported final units are discarded. Policies for other mathematical errors remain open. Use the accepted result ordering for known metre/minute ambiguity and the separate accepted copy/confirmation contracts; ordering for any later added ambiguity must be specified explicitly. Temperature arithmetic is not added by intermediate-unit cancellation.
help.precedence.simpleCompoundUnits.location: Unit powers and compound-unit scope section of operator help and generated documentation previews.

help.precedence.minHeading.meaning: Introduces the shared spelling of the minute alias and the minimum function.
help.precedence.minHeading.context: Help for argument-count disambiguation accepted through contextual-units round 5, including the implied coefficient and min/max minimum arity.
help.precedence.minHeading.location: After duration notation and before unit powers in operator help.

help.precedence.minRule.text: The min function takes at least two arguments separated by semicolons. One complete expression in the following parentheses denotes minutes multiplied by that expression: 2min(2+4) equals 12 minutes. With no coefficient, one minute is implied: min(2+4) = 1min(2+4), or 6 minutes. Two or more arguments denote the function: 2 min(2;4) = 2 * min(2;4) = 4, without a unit. Spaces before min do not change the meaning. Count arguments at the current parentheses level: 2min(max(2;4)) has one outer argument and equals 8 minutes. While 2min(2; is incomplete, the result stays blank. Closing it as 2min(2;) produces a missing-argument error, without reinterpreting the list as minutes. The max function also requires at least two arguments. Other malformed argument lists are still being specified.
help.precedence.minRule.meaning: Explains how min distinguishes the minute unit from the minimum function by its outer argument count, including an implied one-minute coefficient and missing-argument states.
help.precedence.minRule.context: Accepted through contextual-units round 5, superseding one-argument functions min and max. Nested-call separators do not count as outer arguments. The explicitly accepted incomplete min list has no live result, and the closed list with a missing argument is an error. Do not reinterpret it as a minute product. Minute examples express value and dimension, not a new default output spelling. Other malformed lists remain open; this rule does not automatically allow every unit without a coefficient.
help.precedence.minRule.location: Minutes and min function section of operator help and generated previews.

completion.function.min.description.text: Smallest of two or more values.
completion.function.min.description.meaning: Describes the minimum function and its required minimum argument count.
completion.function.min.description.context: Shown when suggesting the min function, whose arguments are separated by semicolons. Contextual-units round 4 changes its minimum arity to two. Unit-alias min is a separate interpretation; this entry describes the function.
completion.function.min.description.location: Immediately after the complete min signature in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. Use the same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, without right-edge alignment.

error.missingArgument.meaning: Explains that an argument position in a closed argument list is empty.
error.missingArgument.context: Approved in contextual-units round 5 for a closed list such as 2min(2;). The incomplete 2min(2; keeps the result blank instead. A closed list with a missing argument must not be reinterpreted as a minute quantity. Other malformed lists and diagnostic precedence remain to be specified.
error.missingArgument.location: The calculation diagnostic region associated with the current expression.

completion.function.max.description.text: Largest of two or more values.
completion.function.max.description.meaning: Describes the maximum function and its required minimum argument count.
completion.function.max.description.context: Shown when suggesting the max function, whose arguments are separated by semicolons. Contextual-units round 5 changes its minimum arity to two. No unit named max is introduced.
completion.function.max.description.location: Immediately after the complete max signature in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. Use the same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, without right-edge alignment.

error.missingOperator.meaning: Explains that an explicit operation is needed between the adjacent quantities.
error.missingOperator.context: Candidate wording for the missing-operator diagnostic accepted in contextual-units round 7: a compound duration followed by a quantity of a clearly different dimension, such as 1h30m2km. The behavior is approved; the exact wording is an editorial draft. Do not use this error to reject the accepted ambiguous 1m30m readings, incomplete 1h30, or other supported implicit multiplication. Diagnostic precedence for unrelated errors remains open.
error.missingOperator.location: The calculation diagnostic region associated with the current expression. Exact character-range highlighting remains part of editor design.

help.copy.quickRule.text: In the quick-mode formula editor with no text selected, press {shortcut} to copy the only displayed current result. Numeric results copy the displayed number without its unit: 4m copies 4. Rounding, all shown digits, grouping and numeral-system prefixes are preserved. With text selected, the shortcut copies that selection, including its unit text. Click a result to copy it. When several results are displayed, the editor has focus and no text is selected, the shortcut leaves the clipboard unchanged and prompts you to choose a result. The calculator stays open, your formula and cursor are preserved, and focus returns to input after a click. Quick copy does not add a history entry.
help.copy.quickRule.meaning: Explains numeric-only result copying, text-selection precedence, the single-entry shortcut condition and choosing among several displayed results.
help.copy.quickRule.context: Accepted through copying round 2. Supply Ctrl+C on Windows and Cmd+C on macOS. A result must be ready and current. A single displayed entry can group several hidden meanings or rounded working values; copying its displayed number does not choose a hidden interpretation. Count the entire grouped result row, including entries outside the horizontal viewport. With editor focus and multiple entries without text selection, preserve the clipboard and show copy.chooseResult. Unit omission applies to numeric quick-copy results, not selected formula text. Numeric prefixes are not units; localized logical results retain their previously approved displayed text. Keyboard selection for confirmation is described in help.confirm.multipleRule. Round 14 accepts copying the highlighted answer while focus is already in the current result row; see help.copy.focusedResultRule. Text-selection precedence in this paragraph applies only while the editor has focus. Known metre/minute result ordering is accepted in round 16; see help.results.orderRule. Feedback geometry remains to be verified. This fragment does not add interpretation captions. This paragraph is scoped to quick-mode editor focus. Round 18 accepts the separate current-expression target and result-row commands in expanded sheets; see help.sheet.copyRule.
help.copy.quickRule.location: Copying section of application help. The help entry point and any compact in-editor hint remain separate interface decisions.

placeholders.shortcut: The platform-specific copy shortcut in its display form; do not translate its key names as ordinary prose.

copy.chooseResult.meaning: Asks the user to identify which displayed result should be copied.
copy.chooseResult.context: Approved in copying round 2. Shown briefly when Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on macOS is pressed in the editor without text selection while more than one current displayed result entry exists. The clipboard is unchanged; no first answer is chosen automatically. A click on a result copies that entry. This is a normal choice state, not a mathematical error. Do not show it for selected formula text or to reinterpret a missing/stale result as a valid answer. Keyboard confirmation selection is now specified in help.confirm.multipleRule. This feedback does not itself enter that selection state or change the accepted editor copy shortcut. Do not show this hint when the current result row already has focus and Ctrl+C/Cmd+C targets its highlighted ready answer; that copy keeps focus in the row. Round 18 also accepts this hint for sheet-editor copy without text selection when the expression containing the cursor has multiple displayed answers, counting the full row including horizontal overflow. Other sheet expressions do not affect that count. See help.sheet.copyRule; the hint does not focus a row by itself.
copy.chooseResult.location: Brief copy feedback associated with the result row; exact placement and keyboard announcement are to be verified without moving the input or adding interpretation captions.

help.confirm.quickRule.text: With one ready displayed result in quick mode, press {shortcut} to record the calculation in history and copy the result. After both succeed, a new empty input starts in the same place, expanded history collapses and the calculator stays open. Arrow Up opens history again with the newest calculation nearest to the input. If saving history or copying fails, the formula and result remain and a brief error appears; the input is not cleared, history does not collapse and the window stays open. Numeric results are copied without units, using the displayed number. Ordinary quick copy keeps your current input and does not add history.
help.confirm.quickRule.meaning: Explains calculation confirmation and its immediate transition to a fresh input, distinguishing it from copying without confirmation.
help.confirm.quickRule.context: Accepted in copying rounds 3 through 5. The default shortcut is Enter in quick mode on both platforms. Full success records history, copies using the existing payload rules, collapses expanded history and focuses empty input in the fixed location. Failure preserves formula, result, open window and history expansion state and shows the appropriate brief error. Empty input has no ready result; do not retain or recopy the previous answer as its result. Enter does not accept completion suggestions. Modified-Enter confirmation is described in help.confirm.hideRule; help.confirm.retryRule explains accepted retry without duplicate history. Copying round 6 accepts the separate selection step for multiple answers; see help.confirm.multipleRule. Operation order, recovery after restart and expanded-mode behavior remain open. Round 16 accepts a new text-undo chain after full successful confirmation starts empty input. Undo in the new calculation does not restore the completed formula or undo its history record or clipboard write. Partial failure preserves the existing input and text-undo chain.
help.confirm.quickRule.location: Calculation confirmation section of application help. This is documentation text, not a new visible button in the quick widget; help entry point remains separate.

placeholders.shortcut: The confirmation shortcut in its platform display form; the accepted default is Enter in quick mode on Windows and macOS.

history.save.error.text: Could not save the calculation to history. Try again.
history.save.error.meaning: Reports that saving a confirmed calculation to history failed.
history.save.error.context: Used when the history-save step of Enter or modified-Enter confirmation in quick mode fails. Keep the formula, result and window open and do not clear input. This error must not imply that copying failed or that an already successful clipboard write has been rolled back. Exact wording is editorial; the brief error and retained input were accepted in copying round 4. Retrying an incomplete confirmation without changing the formula, calculation or chosen answer must not duplicate an already saved history entry; after full success, apply the command used for the retry. Operation order and recovery after restart remain architecture decisions. Failed confirmation also preserves the expanded history state.
history.save.error.location: Brief feedback near the active quick input/result and its accessible error announcement. Exact placement is to be verified without moving the input.

help.confirm.hideRule.text: With one ready displayed result in quick mode, press {shortcut} to record the calculation in history, copy the result and hide the calculator after both succeed. The next invocation starts with empty input. If saving history or copying fails, the formula and result remain, a brief error appears and the window stays open.
help.confirm.hideRule.meaning: Explains the confirmation shortcut that hides the calculator only after successful history saving and result copying.
help.confirm.hideRule.context: Accepted in copying round 4. The default is Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Cmd+Enter on macOS, in quick mode only. Uses the same history action and clipboard payload as Enter; numeric results omit units. Empty input on the next invocation must not retain the previous ready result. This does not change Ctrl+C/Cmd+C or click quick copy. Retry without duplicate history was accepted in copying round 5; see help.confirm.retryRule. Copying round 6 accepts the separate selection step for multiple answers; see help.confirm.multipleRule. The command used on the selected answer determines whether to hide. Operation order, recovery after restart and expanded-mode behavior remain open. The history expansion state on the next invocation after hiding is not yet selected. Native shortcut and focus behavior still require the platform prototype. Round 16 accepts a new text-undo chain after full successful confirmation starts empty input. Undo in the new calculation does not restore the completed formula or undo its history record or clipboard write. Partial failure preserves the existing input and text-undo chain.
help.confirm.hideRule.location: Calculation confirmation section of application help, next to help.confirm.quickRule. Documentation only; this adds no visible button to the quick widget.

placeholders.shortcut: The confirmation-and-hide shortcut in platform display form; accepted defaults are Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Cmd+Enter on macOS, in quick mode.

help.confirm.retryRule.text: If confirmation fails, retry without changing the formula, result or chosen answer to finish the same calculation. An entry already saved to history will not be added again. After saving and copying succeed, the command used for the retry determines whether the calculator stays open with empty input or hides until the next invocation. If you choose a different answer after a failed confirmation and confirm it, that is a new confirmation. Any entry already saved with the previous choice remains unchanged.
help.confirm.retryRule.meaning: Explains retrying a failed calculation confirmation without adding a duplicate history entry.
help.confirm.retryRule.context: Accepted in copying round 5. Applies to retrying incomplete quick-mode confirmation of an unchanged formula, calculation and chosen answer, including when history was saved but clipboard copying failed. Changed formulas or results start a new confirmation. Copying round 8 distinguishes a new successful confirmation after full success: it creates a separate history entry even for identical formula and results. Enter on successful retry starts empty input and collapses history; Ctrl+Enter on Windows / Cmd+Enter on macOS hides with empty input on the next invocation. No atomic transaction or rollback of the system clipboard is promised. Operation order, persistence details and recovery after restart remain architecture decisions. Round 16 explicitly treats confirmation of a different selected displayed answer as a new confirmation even when the formula and full result set are unchanged. Keep an already saved entry with choice A when a later confirmation saves a separate entry with B; do not invent an entry for an earlier save that never succeeded. Selection movement and quick copy alone still create no history. Full successful confirmation starts a fresh text-undo chain; partial failure does not.
help.confirm.retryRule.location: Calculation confirmation section of application help, following the normal and hide confirmation explanations. Documentation only; no new retry button in the quick widget is approved.

help.confirm.multipleRule.text: When quick mode shows several results, press {confirmShortcut} or {hideShortcut} to focus the result row. The first answer is highlighted, but nothing is copied or saved yet. Use Left Arrow and Right Arrow to choose; the row scrolls when needed and stops at either end without wrapping. Up Arrow and Down Arrow leave result selection and immediately navigate history as usual, without copying or confirming. Press {confirmShortcut} again to record the calculation and copy the chosen answer, then start empty input with history collapsed. Press {hideShortcut} instead to confirm and hide the calculator. Escape returns the cursor to its previous position in the formula without changes. Clicking an answer still only copies it and returns focus to input. Typing, pasting, Backspace or Delete returns you to the formula at the previous cursor or text selection and performs the usual edit. This ends result selection and recalculates without copying or recording; Backspace and Delete edit formula text, not history.
help.confirm.multipleRule.meaning: Explains choosing one displayed answer with the keyboard before confirming a calculation that has several results.
help.confirm.multipleRule.context: Accepted in copying round 6 for quick mode. Entry into selection does not record history, copy, reset input or hide; highlighting the first answer is navigation focus only. Completion closes without accepting a suggestion. The command used on the selected answer determines the successful transition. Existing numeric copy payload, confirmation failure and unchanged-calculation retry rules still apply. Selection of a grouped displayed answer does not discard hidden interpretations. This does not change Ctrl+C/Cmd+C in the formula editor or approve result captions. Copying round 7 accepts saving the complete result set and the displayed answer chosen at confirmation; see help.history.recordRule. Round 14 accepts copying while retaining row focus (help.copy.focusedResultRule) and returning to normal formula editing on typing, paste, Backspace or Delete. Perform the edit at the restored cursor/selection, end answer selection and apply normal live-result invalidation; do not retain an old ready result for changed, incomplete or erroneous input. This does not assign those keys in history search, menus or sheets. Round 15 accepts stopping Left/Right at the current row boundaries and exiting selection to perform ordinary history navigation on the same Up/Down keypress. This does not assign arrow behavior in search, menus or calculation sheets. Storage format, other remaining keys and result changes outside this editing transition remain separate decisions; native focus and accessibility require prototype verification. Round 16 fixes the known m/metre-minute interpretation order in help.results.orderRule, and clarifies direct Up/Down recall with return to the original input in help.history.navigationRule. The proposed separate Tab history-view context was not accepted.
help.confirm.multipleRule.location: Calculation confirmation section of application help, after the single-answer and hide command explanations. Describes the existing result row; no new menu or button is added.

placeholders.confirmShortcut: The normal quick-mode confirmation shortcut in platform display form; the accepted default is Enter on Windows and macOS.
placeholders.hideShortcut: The quick-mode confirmation-and-hide shortcut in platform display form; accepted defaults are Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Cmd+Enter on macOS.

help.history.recordRule.text: History keeps the formula, all its results and the answer chosen when you confirmed the calculation. Copying one answer does not remove the others. Saved results do not change when you edit a constant or function. When you bring a formula back into input, it is calculated again using the current definitions; the original history entry stays unchanged. Bringing a formula back into input does not itself add a new history entry. Each new successful confirmation adds a separate history entry, even for an identical calculation. Retrying an unfinished confirmation after an error does not duplicate its saved entry. If a saved definition was renamed, recalling its formula uses the current name of that same definition; the original history text and answers remain unchanged. After a definition is deleted, recalculation may require restoring it or correcting the formula.
help.history.recordRule.meaning: Explains what a history record retains and distinguishes viewing saved results from recalculating a recalled formula.
help.history.recordRule.context: Accepted in copying round 7. Records retain working values and hidden interpretations as well as the displayed answer chosen at confirmation, not merely the rounded unitless clipboard text. Historical values are not recalculated when definitions change; recalling a formula into input uses current definitions. Locale changes may redraw local unit symbols under the existing language rule without changing historical values. Copying round 8 accepts a row containing the formula and all saved displayed results, with the confirmation choice in bold and horizontal overflow; see help.history.displayRule. Every new successful confirmation creates a separate entry even for identical content; retrying an unfinished confirmation after failure must not duplicate its entry. This does not approve a new badge or button, automatic restoration of old definitions, or a serialization format. Under round 16, an unchanged retry also requires the same chosen displayed answer. Confirming a different answer after partial failure creates a new entry and preserves any entry already saved with the previous choice. Round 18 accepts semantic rename handling on structured recall into quick input or a sheet: preserve the historical source text and values, but adapt references to the current name of the same definition. Reusing its former name for another definition must not hijack that binding. Ordinary selected-text copying retains visible original text. History alone does not block deletion of a global definition; no automatic substitution of an unrelated same-named replacement is approved.
help.history.recordRule.location: History section of application help, alongside the explanation of recalling calculations. Documentation text; the history row and its accessible presentation are specified separately.

history.result.chosen.meaning: Identifies the historical answer selected when the calculation was confirmed.
history.result.chosen.context: Editorial accessibility description for the saved selected answer when a history entry has several displayed answers. Copying round 8 accepts visual bold emphasis; this description communicates its meaning to assistive technology. It describes the original confirmation choice, not current keyboard focus or a later click. No visible interpretation caption or badge is added. Exact native announcement and integration with the full history entry require prototype verification.
history.result.chosen.location: Programmatic description of the chosen historical answer inside a history row; not visible text.

help.history.displayRule.text: Each history row shows the formula and all its saved results. With several results, the answer chosen at confirmation is bold. Long rows scroll horizontally. Moving through history does not change the saved choice.
help.history.displayRule.meaning: Explains the history row, its saved choice emphasis and access to long content.
help.history.displayRule.context: Accepted in copying round 8. All saved displayed answers are shown after the existing grouping of identical full formatted answers, retaining hidden interpretations. Interpretation captions remain absent. A single displayed answer needs no additional choice emphasis. Bold emphasis must preserve the existing dim fractional tail. Saved choice is distinct from current keyboard focus. Exact visual styling and accessibility remain subject to prototype verification. Clicking a saved answer copies it under the rule accepted in round 15; see help.history.copyRule. The clicked target does not have to be the answer shown in bold, and copying does not change that saved choice.
help.history.displayRule.location: History section of application help, next to help.history.recordRule. Documentation only; no new history control is introduced.

history.undo.meaning: Restores the most recent history deletion or whole-history clearing operation that has not yet been undone.
history.undo.context: Copying round 10 accepts undoing deletions in reverse order until the application fully exits, including whole-history clearing as one operation. Hiding and reopening the window preserve Undo. Restore full removed records in their former order without removing calculations added later. Undo from the previous session is unavailable after a full exit. This is separate from formula text undo. Accepted in copying rounds 9 and 10. Undo has no short timer while the application remains running. Copying round 13 places this action in the shared history menu. It requires an undoable deletion or clear from the current session and can remain available when the history is empty. Menu geometry, failure feedback and exact unavailable presentation still require verification; this does not assign formula editor undo shortcuts to history.
history.undo.location: Item in the shared history menu; applies to undoable history operations rather than the current formula text.

history.clear.description.text: This will clear your calculation history. Your constants, functions, sheets and templates will be kept. You can undo the clearing until you fully quit the application.
history.clear.description.meaning: Explains the scope of clearing history and the other data that will be preserved.
history.clear.description.context: Editorial text for the whole-history confirmation accepted in copying round 9. Shown with history.clear.title before confirmation. Copying round 10 accepts undoing clearing until the application fully exits, including after the window is hidden and reopened. Do not promise Undo after a full exit or erase newer calculations when undoing a clear.
history.clear.description.location: Body of the calculation-history clearing confirmation dialog.

history.clear.confirm.meaning: Confirms the pending request to clear the entire calculation history.
history.clear.confirm.context: Primary confirmation action in the history-clearing dialog accepted in copying round 9. The user must explicitly activate it before clearing history; common.cancel dismisses the pending action. Does not delete constants, functions, sheets or templates. Exact focus and failure behavior remain to be designed.
history.clear.confirm.location: Confirmation action in the calculation-history clearing dialog.

help.history.searchRule.text: In quick mode, press {shortcut} to search history by formula or saved result. Type any part of a formula or saved displayed result; matching ignores letter case. Matches update as you type and keep the normal history order. An empty query shows all history. Up Arrow and Down Arrow choose a record while preserving your formula. Enter closes search and brings the chosen formula into input for recalculation without confirming or copying it. Escape closes search and restores your previous formula and cursor. With no matches, Enter recalls nothing. The formula input stays in place, and searching does not recalculate saved results.
help.history.searchRule.meaning: Explains opening history search while preserving the current formula draft.
help.history.searchRule.context: Accepted in copying rounds 9 through 11. Default is Ctrl+F on Windows and Cmd+F on macOS inside active quick mode. Search has its own key context: navigation does not recall a formula until Enter, and this Enter is not calculation confirmation. Normal history navigation outside search keeps its accepted behavior. Escape restores the original draft and cursor. This does not set expanded-editor search behavior. Copying round 11 accepts case-insensitive substring matching in the formula or any saved displayed result. Matches retain the normal history order; an empty query shows the entire history. This does not change case-sensitive expression semantics or recalculate saved values. Copying round 12 accepts decimal point/comma and numeric digit-grouping equivalents, plus plain/superscript 2/3 in recognized length-unit area/volume spellings in the Latin baseline and active locale. Preserve ordinary substring matches and stored text. Do not normalize caret exponentiation into unit shorthand, rewrite names/comments, evaluate formulas or convert units/bases. See help.history.searchNotationRule. Exact field placement remains open.
help.history.searchRule.location: History section of application help, alongside history viewing and recall instructions.

placeholders.shortcut: The history-search shortcut in platform display form; accepted defaults are Ctrl+F on Windows and Cmd+F on macOS in quick mode.

help.history.manageRule.text: Deleting one history entry requires no confirmation. Clearing the entire history requires confirmation. Undo restores deletions in reverse order; clearing the entire history counts as one operation. You can undo until you fully quit the application. Hiding and reopening the window keeps Undo available. Restoring removed entries keeps calculations added later. These actions preserve your constants, functions, sheets and templates. History Undo is separate from undoing formula text edits.
help.history.manageRule.meaning: Explains the difference between deleting a history record and clearing the complete history.
help.history.manageRule.context: Accepted in copying rounds 9 and 10. Deletion targets a specific record rather than matching content. Undo restores complete records with working values, hidden interpretations and the original chosen answer in their former order. Full-history clearing is undone as one operation without deleting newer records. Undo remains available while the application runs, without a short timer; no previous-session Undo is promised after full exit. Ctrl+Z/Cmd+Z in the formula editor continue to undo text only. Copying round 11 accepts keeping the entire history across launches until manual deletion, without age or record-count expiry. This retention is separate from session-limited Undo. Copying round 13 supplies control access through the shared history menu; see help.history.menuRule. Menu presentation and error behavior remain open.
help.history.manageRule.location: History management section of application help.

help.history.retentionRule.text: Your history is kept between application launches until you delete it. Old entries are not removed automatically because of their age or the number of saved calculations. Undo for deletions and clearing is available only until you fully quit the application.
help.history.retentionRule.meaning: Explains durable history retention and distinguishes it from the shorter availability of deletion Undo.
help.history.retentionRule.context: Accepted in copying round 11. The entire history is retained without automatic age or record-count cleanup; manually deleted records do not reappear on an ordinary relaunch. Search and history access cover all saved records, not only currently loaded or visible rows. Full application exit ends Undo availability under round 10 while leaving the remaining history saved. This does not select a storage format, require loading all records into memory, or promise recovery of deleted records after exit.
help.history.retentionRule.location: History section of application help, next to history management and Undo rules.

help.history.searchNotationRule.text: History search treats 1,5 and 1.5, and 1000 and 1 000, as equivalent number spellings. It also matches unit spellings such as m2 and m², or cm3 and cm³, in either direction. Caret powers such as 2m^2 remain distinct from unit shorthand such as 2m2. Search can match any saved displayed answer as well as the formula.
help.history.searchNotationRule.meaning: Explains the accepted number-format and unit-power spelling equivalents used by history search.
help.history.searchNotationRule.context: Accepted in copying round 12. Decimal separators and digit grouping are normalized only in recognized decimal number fragments. Unit equivalents follow the existing whole-symbol length-unit shorthand rule, including explicit aliases, Latin symbols and the active locale. Do not rewrite user names or comments, normalize arbitrary word prefixes, remove nonnumeric whitespace, evaluate formulas, convert bases or convert quantities. Ordinary case-insensitive substring matches remain available. Caret distinction applies to the spelling comparison, not exclusion of a history record that independently matches a saved displayed result. Storage, values, hidden interpretations, choice and ordering stay unchanged.
help.history.searchNotationRule.location: History search section of application help, next to help.history.searchRule.

history.menu.accessibleName.meaning: Names the popup menu for working with individual records and the complete history.
history.menu.accessibleName.context: Editorial programmatic name for the shared menu accepted in copying round 13. The visible actions are history.reuse, history.delete, history.undo and history.clear. The menu opens by right-clicking a record or the local quick-mode shortcut, including when history is collapsed or empty. Individual actions require a target entry; general actions follow their existing eligibility rules. No new visible heading or permanent toolbar is approved. Native announcement and placement need prototype verification.
history.menu.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of the shared history popup menu.

help.history.menuRule.text: In quick mode, right-click a history entry or press {shortcut} to open the history menu. Use formula and Delete entry apply to a chosen record. Undo restores the last deletion or clearing operation. Clear history asks for confirmation. The shortcut also works when history is collapsed or empty; record actions require a selected entry. Opening the menu leaves your formula unchanged. Escape closes it and restores the previous focus.
help.history.menuRule.meaning: Explains how to open the shared history menu and which commands need a particular history record.
help.history.menuRule.context: Accepted in copying round 13. The local shortcut is Ctrl+Shift+H on Windows and Cmd+Shift+H on macOS inside active quick mode. Right-click targets a record without copying, recalling or confirming it. Use formula recalls a copy for recalculation only. Undo follows session-limited reverse-order recovery and can remain available after a clear; Clear history still requires confirmation. Menu opening does not execute a command. Placement, unavailable-item appearance, native shortcuts and focus still require prototype verification. This adds no permanent toolbar.
help.history.menuRule.location: History management section of application help, next to help.history.manageRule.

placeholders.shortcut: The local quick-mode history-menu shortcut in platform display form; accepted defaults are Ctrl+Shift+H on Windows and Cmd+Shift+H on macOS.

help.copy.focusedResultRule.text: While the current result row has focus, press {shortcut} to copy the highlighted answer. Numbers copy without units, using the displayed formatting. Focus and selection stay on that answer; your formula, cursor and window are preserved, and no history entry is added. You can then press Enter to confirm or Escape to return to the formula. A text selection left in the editor does not change which answer is copied.
help.copy.focusedResultRule.meaning: Explains keyboard copying of a highlighted current answer while preserving result selection.
help.copy.focusedResultRule.context: Accepted in copying round 14 for quick-mode current results. Supply Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on macOS. The highlighted displayed answer must be ready and current. Use the same payload rules as editor quick copy: displayed numeric text without units, retaining shown digits, rounding, signs, grouping, base prefix and letter case; logical results keep their visible localized text. Copying does not choose a latent interpretation, record history, reset input or hide the window. Active focus determines the shortcut target even when the inactive formula editor retains a text selection. Clipboard feedback reflects the actual write. Clicking a current answer instead returns focus to input. This does not define copying with focus in historical results, search, menus or calculation sheets.
help.copy.focusedResultRule.location: Copying section of application help, next to the formula-editor shortcut rule and the explanation of keyboard result selection.

placeholders.shortcut: The platform-specific copy shortcut in its display form: Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on macOS.

help.history.copyRule.text: Click an answer in history to copy its saved displayed value. Numbers copy without units, retaining displayed formatting; logical answers copy their displayed text. Your current formula and cursor are preserved, focus returns to input and the calculator stays open. This does not recalculate, confirm, add a history entry or change the answer chosen at confirmation. If a saved calculation shows price * 2 = 200, clicking its answer copies 200 even if the current price would give 300. Use formula brings the expression into input for a new calculation.
help.history.copyRule.meaning: Explains copying a saved historical answer while keeping the current input and the historical calculation unchanged.
help.history.copyRule.context: Accepted in copying round 15 for clicking a particular displayed answer in quick-mode history. Use the clicked saved answer, including when it was not chosen at confirmation or requires horizontal scrolling to reach. Preserve the historical values and hidden interpretations. Apply the common result-copy payload rules: numeric displayed text without units, including rounding, all shown digits, sign, grouping and numeral-system prefix/case; logical values keep their displayed localized text. Changed definitions do not invalidate a historical answer or trigger evaluation on copy. The example uses the user-defined constant price; its local equivalent may be used in translation. Use formula refers to history.reuse, which separately recalls the expression and recalculates using current definitions. Clipboard feedback reflects the actual write. This fragment does not assign a keyboard copy target inside history, change search navigation or define copying in calculation sheets. Keyboard copy in history opened from an expanded sheet was accepted separately in round 17; see help.history.extendedShortcutRule. This click-copy fragment remains scoped to its original interaction.
help.history.copyRule.location: History and copying sections of application help, near the explanation of saved values and recalling formulas. Describes clicks on existing answer values; no new button or interpretation caption is introduced.

help.history.navigationRule.text: In quick mode, Up Arrow opens history and immediately brings the preceding calculation into input. Press Up again to recall older entries while the list moves downward through the fixed input. Down Arrow moves back through the entries until it restores the text you had before browsing, even if that text was not empty. Recalled formulas are calculated again using the current definitions; saved history entries stay unchanged. Returning to your original input restores its cursor and collapses history. Up stops at the oldest entry, and further Down at your original input does not clear it.
help.history.navigationRule.meaning: Explains direct console history recall and returning to the original quick input.
help.history.navigationRule.context: Accepted in copying round 16 as the user replacement for the proposed Tab history-view mode. Preserve the original text and cursor/selection from the start of browsing; repeated recalls do not overwrite that navigation snapshot. An open completion menu retains its existing arrow priority. Recall and return are text-undo steps under help.input.undoRule and do not confirm, copy or add history. The saved record is unchanged. The previous unconditional empty-input return is superseded. Round 17 accepts collapse on return to any original input with cursor/selection restoration, Up stopping at the oldest entry, and Down preserving the original input once reached. This is quick-mode navigation; history search keeps its own accepted no-recall-until-Enter behavior.
help.history.navigationRule.location: History navigation section of application help, near the quick-input and recall explanations. Describes the existing fixed input and history region; no Tab-only mode or new visible control is added.

help.input.undoRule.text: Each formula recalled from history and each Down Arrow return to your original input is one text-undo step. Press {shortcut} to restore the previous text and cursor; the formula is recalculated with the current definitions. This also applies when you use a search result or Use formula. A new empty input after successful confirmation starts a separate undo chain. Undo does not remove saved calculations or undo a clipboard copy. Hiding the window keeps text undo available; fully quitting ends that chain. Copying a sheet result does not start a new text-undo chain.
help.input.undoRule.meaning: Explains text undo for history recall and its boundary between confirmed quick calculations and application sessions.
help.input.undoRule.context: Accepted in copying round 16, points 1-3, with the direct original-input return correction from point 5 taking precedence over the old unconditional empty return. Use Ctrl+Z on Windows and Cmd+Z on macOS. Restore the prior text and cursor/selection as one undo step for each recall or actual original-input return. Merely selecting a search result does not mutate input. Revisiting a history entry recalls its saved formula; unsaved edits can be recovered through text undo. This does not alter the separate undo of history deletions. Only full successful confirmation starts the next calculation and new undo chain; a partial failure does not. Extended-sheet editing and crash recovery are separate decisions. Round 17 separately accepts inserting a historical formula into an expanded sheet as one ordinary editing action; see help.history.extendedShortcutRule. This does not apply quick-mode confirmation resets to sheet editing. Round 18 explicitly keeps the sheet text-undo chain when copying results. Recalled formulas adapt semantically bound renamed global references under help.definitions.renameRule. Definition deletion Undo remains distinct from both text undo and history deletion Undo.
help.input.undoRule.location: Text editing and history navigation sections of application help; no new action label or button is introduced.

placeholders.shortcut: The platform-specific text-undo shortcut: Ctrl+Z on Windows or Cmd+Z on macOS.

help.quick.restoreRule.text: After you fully quit and reopen the application, quick mode restores your last input and cursor, with history collapsed and focus in the input. The formula is calculated again using the current definitions. If your last input was empty, it stays empty. Text undo from the previous application session is not restored. Simply hiding and reopening the window keeps the current text-undo chain.
help.quick.restoreRule.meaning: Explains normal-restart persistence of quick input separately from text undo.
help.quick.restoreRule.context: Accepted in copying round 16, point 3. Persist the last quick-input text and cursor/selection for normal full exit and restart. Recalculate restored input with current definitions and normal incomplete/error behavior; do not expose a stored old result as a newly ready answer. Start with history collapsed, editor focus and no restored result-selection, search or menu state. This does not decide crash recovery, persistence of the original-input navigation snapshot during interrupted browsing, or the lifecycle of calculation sheets. Ordinary window hiding is not a full application exit.
help.quick.restoreRule.location: Application lifecycle and quick-input sections of help; no launch dialog or new visible control is added.

help.results.orderRule.text: Possible answers follow a fixed interpretation order. For m, metre comes before minute; ambiguous occurrences are considered from left to right. Thus 10m / 2s shows 5m/s before 300. Removing invalid alternatives keeps the remaining order; identical displayed answers share the position of their first alternative. Changing numbers or the interface language does not sort answers into a different order.
help.results.orderRule.meaning: Explains stable ordering and first-position display grouping for the accepted metre/minute ambiguity.
help.results.orderRule.context: Accepted in copying round 16, point 4. Known ambiguous occurrences use metre before minute and occur left to right in source; combinations follow the corresponding sequential interpretation order. Filtering preserves relative order and grouping uses the first constituent position while preserving all hidden meanings and working values. The Russian alias follows the same identity order. This is a presentation contract, not a mandated evaluation algorithm or a choice of one hidden interpretation. Source changes may change the alternatives; other ambiguity kinds require an explicit ordering extension if later included. Existing no-caption and horizontal-overflow rules remain in effect.
help.results.orderRule.location: Result interpretation section of application help, next to grouping and alternative-answer explanations. No visible ranking number or interpretation caption is added.

help.history.extendedShortcutRule.text: In expanded mode, press {shortcut} with either modifier key to open history while keeping your sheet unchanged. Up Arrow and Down Arrow choose a record; Left Arrow and Right Arrow choose its saved answer. Start at the latest record and its answer chosen at confirmation; when you change records, select that record’s confirmation choice. Navigation stops at the ends and scrolls the selected item into view. Press {copyShortcut} to copy the saved answer without recalculation and keep focus in history. Enter closes history and inserts the formula at your previous cursor, replacing selected text, as one ordinary edit. The sheet recalculates without confirming or adding history. Escape or {shortcut} again closes history without insertion and restores the previous cursor. Empty history provides nothing to select or insert. Ordinary arrows retain text-editor behavior while editing. References to renamed saved definitions use their current names in the inserted formula; the history record stays unchanged.
help.history.extendedShortcutRule.meaning: Explains opening, navigating, copying and inserting from history while preserving the expanded sheet until insertion.
help.history.extendedShortcutRule.context: Alt+Up with either physical modifier was accepted in round 16; the complete interaction was accepted in round 17, point 2. Use platform Alt/Option naming and Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on macOS. Opening transfers focus to history while retaining sheet text and cursor/selection. Preserve saved record values and confirmation choices; navigation focus is not a stored-choice mutation. Use the existing numeric displayed text without units and localized logical text for clipboard copy; copying retains history focus and does not recalculate. Enter inserts the saved formula text at the retained cursor or replaces the retained selection in one ordinary edit, closes history, returns editor focus and triggers normal sheet recalculation without confirming or recording. An insertion producing incomplete or invalid input follows ordinary evaluation rules and does not reuse stale answers. Escape or repeated Alt+Up closes without insertion. Empty history cannot target a nonexistent record. This is a separate context from quick console recall, history search and completion navigation. Native focus, placement and accessibility remain to be verified. Per-line results, sheet autosave and local shadowing of global constants were accepted separately in points 4-6; see the sheet help fragments. Copying a newly calculated sheet result was accepted in round 18; see help.sheet.copyRule. Structured history insertion adapts references to renamed saved definitions to their current names while preserving the original history record, under help.definitions.renameRule.
help.history.extendedShortcutRule.location: Expanded-mode keyboard help, alongside the history-opening action. The final help entry point and history placement remain interface work.

placeholders.shortcut: The accepted Alt+Up Arrow history-opening shortcut in platform display form, using the platform Alt/Option key name and accepting either physical modifier key.
placeholders.copyShortcut: The platform-specific result-copy shortcut: Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on macOS.

help.sheet.dependenciesRule.text: In a calculation sheet, define each local variable once. Expressions may reference definitions farther down the sheet: total = price * quantity can precede price = 100 and quantity = 3 and still gives 300. Editing a definition recalculates its dependent expressions. Defining the same local name again is an error. Circular dependencies block the expressions in the cycle and those that depend on them; independent expressions still calculate. Multiline user-function bodies keep their sequential execution rules.
help.sheet.dependenciesRule.meaning: Explains the accepted dependency model for sheet variables and its scope relative to function bodies.
help.sheet.dependenciesRule.context: Accepted in round 17, point 3. One sheet-local definition per name, forward references permitted, dependency-driven recalculation and explicit cycle handling. Reject duplicate local definitions rather than silently choosing first or last. Do not mark nonparticipating downstream expressions as themselves cyclic; they are blocked by a required value. Example identifiers may be localized in explanatory prose and do not create reserved names. Points 4-6 were subsequently accepted for sheets: see help.sheet.resultsRule, help.sheet.scopeRule and help.sheet.autosaveRule. These are separate from sequential function bodies and explicit global-definition saving. Global definition storage, name resolution and function dependencies remain their own domain contracts within the shared calculation core.
help.sheet.dependenciesRule.location: Calculation-sheet language section of application help, distinct from the sequential user-function body explanation.

sheet.duplicateVariable.text: Variable {name} is defined more than once in this sheet.
sheet.duplicateVariable.meaning: Reports a duplicate local variable definition in a calculation sheet.
sheet.duplicateVariable.context: Editorial wording for the duplicate-definition error accepted in round 17, point 3. Use when a sheet contains more than one local definition of the same name under the accepted case-sensitive naming rules. Do not reinterpret the duplicate as a sequential reassignment. This is not a rule rejecting a same-named global constant; point 5 now accepts sheet-local shadowing of a saved constant without changing that constant. Round 18 separately rejects sheet-local names matching saved user functions; use sheet.functionNameConflict for that case. It does not govern editing or saving a global definition or assignment inside a sequential function body.
sheet.duplicateVariable.location: Diagnostic associated with duplicate definitions in the calculation-sheet editor; exact highlighting and accessible announcement remain interface work.

placeholders.name: The duplicate sheet-local variable name as written by the user; preserve its spelling and case.

sheet.dependencyError.text: A required value could not be calculated.
sheet.dependencyError.meaning: Explains why a sheet expression cannot calculate when a required dependency is blocked.
sheet.dependencyError.context: Editorial wording for an expression blocked by a required dependency under rounds 17 and 18. A dependency with an error or incomplete input has no ready value; do not show a stale value as current. A downstream expression need not itself participate in a cycle. Independent expressions continue calculating. Do not present transient incomplete input itself as a mathematical error; the affected incomplete expression has no ready answer. Preserve lazy if/and/or behavior for unused branches. Recovery of expression boundaries after malformed syntax and conditional-cycle analysis remain technical language work.
sheet.dependencyError.location: Diagnostic associated with a sheet expression that cannot obtain a required dependency; exact presentation remains interface work.

help.sheet.resultsRule.text: Each completed expression or assignment in a calculation sheet shows its own result. For example, price = 100 shows 100 and price * 3 shows 300. Blank lines and comments have no result. If an expression has several valid answers, show them all using the existing grouping, ordering and horizontal-scrolling rules.
help.sheet.resultsRule.meaning: Explains results for each calculable sheet expression or assignment.
help.sheet.resultsRule.context: Accepted in round 17, point 4 after scope clarification. This applies to expanded sheets, not intermediate statements inside a saved function body. Preserve all underlying meanings and working values when displayed answers are grouped. A completed but invalid expression must not expose a stale ready answer. Copy commands were accepted in round 18; see help.sheet.copyRule. Exact placement and font treatment remain interface work; this paragraph does not approve a right-hand result column.
help.sheet.resultsRule.location: Expanded-sheet result section of application help, near the sheet dependency explanation. The visual placement of per-expression results still requires prototype review.

help.sheet.scopeRule.text: Local variables belong to their calculation sheet. They do not become saved definitions in quick mode or other sheets. A local variable takes precedence over a saved constant with the same name inside that sheet without changing the saved constant. If the global price is 50 and a sheet defines price = 100, that sheet uses 100 while quick mode still uses 50. Built-in names remain protected. A sheet-local name cannot match a saved function name. Saved functions do not implicitly use the calling sheet’s local variables.
help.sheet.scopeRule.meaning: Explains sheet-local variable scope and shadowing of a saved user constant.
help.sheet.scopeRule.context: Accepted in round 17, point 5 after scope clarification. Global saved constants are not overwritten by sheet editing or autosave. Existing built-in identifier protection remains unchanged. Example names may be localized in help prose without changing users’ identifiers. Round 18 accepts an error for sheet-local names matching saved functions and the saved-function environment of parameters, own sequential local intermediates and saved global definitions. Arguments evaluate in the caller context before binding. See help.definitions.functionScopeRule and help.definitions.namesRule. This does not impose global uniqueness on every function parameter or local intermediate.
help.sheet.scopeRule.location: Expanded-sheet variable section of application help, distinct from the saved-definition library help.

help.sheet.autosaveRule.text: You can keep several named calculation sheets. Their text is saved automatically on this computer, including unfinished or erroneous expressions. Autosaving does not add calculation-history entries. Reopening a sheet restores its text and calculates it again using the current saved constants and functions. Saving a template and saving a global constant or function remain separate actions.
help.sheet.autosaveRule.meaning: Explains local autosave of named sheet documents and recalculation on reopening.
help.sheet.autosaveRule.context: Accepted in round 17, point 6 after scope clarification. Save sheet text independently of calculation success; the data model must distinguish a persisted erroneous draft from a failed persistence operation. Reopening does not present an old cached answer as a newly evaluated result. This behavior does not autosave or publish global definition edits and does not choose template update semantics. Exact storage format, management controls, persistence timing, retry and crash recovery remain architecture or product decisions; do not imply verified durability guarantees from this help paragraph.
help.sheet.autosaveRule.location: Sheet persistence section of application help, alongside named-sheet management. This explains automatic saving and does not introduce a manual Save sheet button.

help.sheet.copyRule.text: In the sheet editor, Enter inserts a new line. With text selected, {copyShortcut} copies the selection. Without a selection, it copies the only ready displayed answer of the expression containing the cursor. If that expression has several answers, the clipboard stays unchanged and you are prompted to choose a result. Click an answer to copy it. Press {resultShortcut} to copy the current expression’s single answer or focus its result row to choose with Left and Right. In that row, Enter or {resultShortcut} copies the chosen answer and returns to the previous editor cursor; {copyShortcut} copies it while keeping row focus. Escape returns without copying. Typing, paste, Backspace or Delete resumes normal editing at the previous cursor or selection. Numeric answers copy the displayed number without units, preserving shown rounding, digits, sign, grouping and base prefix and case. Logical answers copy their visible localized text. Missing, invalid or stale answers cannot be copied. The sheet stays open and is not cleared. Copying, recalculation and autosave do not add history entries or reset text undo.
help.sheet.copyRule.meaning: Explains current-expression copying and result-row focus in an expanded calculation sheet.
help.sheet.copyRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 1. Supply Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Enter on Windows, Cmd+C and Cmd+Enter on macOS. Count the complete grouped displayed result set of the expression containing the editor cursor, including horizontal overflow, not all sheet results. Preserve underlying meanings when display entries group. Inactive editor selection does not override a focused answer row. The common history records quick-mode confirmations, not sheet copy or autosave. History opened by Alt+Up retains its separate Enter-for-insertion context. Do not inherit quick-mode clearing, hiding or confirmation undo resets. Other row keys, result placement and native focus still need design or verification.
help.sheet.copyRule.location: Expanded-sheet copying section of application help; not a new permanent control in the editor.

placeholders.copyShortcut: Platform copy command: Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on macOS.
placeholders.resultShortcut: Platform sheet-result command: Ctrl+Enter on Windows or Cmd+Enter on macOS.

help.sheet.errorRule.text: An expression with an error or incomplete input has no ready result. Expressions depending on it also have no ready answer; independent expressions continue calculating. For a = 1 / 0, b = a + 1 and c = 2 + 2, a has an error, b cannot obtain its dependency and c is 4. An unknown-name message identifies the name. Previous values are never presented as current results. The sheet still saves your text. Unused branches of if, and and or are not evaluated.
help.sheet.errorRule.meaning: Explains how sheet errors and incomplete values affect dependents while independent calculations remain available.
help.sheet.errorRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 2. Apply to distinguishable expressions and their dependencies. Incomplete input does not by itself warrant a mathematical error message; keep the ready result absent. Use expression.unknownName for unresolved names and sheet.dependencyError for a blocked required dependency. Parser recovery and conditional-cycle analysis remain technical design work.
help.sheet.errorRule.location: Expanded-sheet error and dependency section of application help.

help.definitions.functionScopeRule.text: A saved function uses its parameters, its own local intermediate names and saved global definitions. It does not implicitly use the calling sheet’s local variables. With global price = 50 and cost(x) = x * price, a sheet-local price = 100 does not change cost(2): the answer is 100. To use a sheet value inside a function, pass it as an argument. Arguments are calculated in the caller’s context before they bind to parameters. Multiline function bodies run in order.
help.definitions.functionScopeRule.meaning: Explains the saved-function name environment and explicit passing of caller-local values.
help.definitions.functionScopeRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 3. Preserve sheet-local shadowing of saved constants in direct sheet expressions, sequential function bodies and the last-expression return rule. Example identifiers may be localized in documentation, not by renaming user definitions. This is name scope; exact ambiguous-value propagation remains a separate language contract.
help.definitions.functionScopeRule.location: Saved-function section of application help, next to parameter and multiline examples.

help.definitions.constantRule.text: A saved constant retains its definition formula and its dependencies on other saved constants. With rate = 20% and factor = 1 + rate, explicitly saving rate as 10% changes factor to 1.1. Editing a draft does not change the saved definition before you save it. Cyclic definitions are not allowed.
help.definitions.constantRule.meaning: Explains live formula dependencies of saved constants and their explicit publication boundary.
help.definitions.constantRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 4. Do not freeze a constant to a rounded or unitless clipboard snapshot. Implementation storage and caching are unchosen. This paragraph does not settle propagation of ambiguous units or result sets through definitions.
help.definitions.constantRule.location: Saved-constant section of application help, alongside definition examples.

help.definitions.saveRule.text: Edit a saved definition as a draft, then choose Save to apply it. A valid saved change updates future calculations and recalculates current quick input and open dependent sheets. Invalid syntax, unknown references, recursion or cyclic dependencies keep the previous working version; your edits remain available to correct. A valid function may still fail for particular arguments: f(x) = 1 / x fails at zero. The description from the header’s first # comment is saved with the definition. Existing history answers do not recalculate.
help.definitions.saveRule.meaning: Explains draft editing, explicit publication, validation failures and affected calculations.
help.definitions.saveRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 5. Reuse common.save for the explicit Save command. Header descriptions remain derived from the definition text, not an independently autosaved field. Validation is not exhaustive evaluation for all arguments. Disk-failure behavior and publication atomicity still require technical design. Do not treat sheet autosave as permission to publish global definitions.
help.definitions.saveRule.location: Saved-definition editing section of application help.

help.definitions.namesRule.text: Each global name identifies one saved constant or function. Functions cannot share a name by accepting different numbers of arguments. Creating a definition does not overwrite an existing one; open it explicitly to edit. A sheet-local variable may shadow a saved constant, but it cannot use a saved function’s name. Built-in names remain protected.
help.definitions.namesRule.meaning: Explains global definition uniqueness, explicit editing and sheet-local name conflicts.
help.definitions.namesRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 6, under the existing case-sensitive identifier rules. This does not impose global uniqueness on parameters or intermediate locals belonging to separate function bodies. Function-body local conflict details remain part of language design.
help.definitions.namesRule.location: Naming section of saved-definition help, with a reference from sheet-variable help.

help.definitions.renameRule.text: Renaming a saved definition updates references to it in other saved definitions, sheets and templates. Unrelated local names and comments are unchanged. History keeps its original formula and answers; recalling the formula for a new calculation uses the definition’s current name. Renaming price to cost leaves price * 2 in history but recalls cost * 2. Reusing the old name for another definition does not redirect those references. Name conflicts are checked before the rename; a rename cannot be partially applied.
help.definitions.renameRule.meaning: Explains semantic rename propagation while preserving historical source text and values.
help.definitions.renameRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 7. Update references bound to the definition, not plain string matches, homonymous locals, comments or arbitrary text. Apply adapting recall through console history, history search, Use formula and sheet insertion. Ordinary copied selected historical text stays as visibly written. Validate target conflicts before mutation. Stable identifiers, partial-document bindings and atomic storage require architecture work; the help states intended behavior, not completed verification.
help.definitions.renameRule.location: Rename section of saved-definition management help.

help.definitions.deleteRule.text: A definition cannot be deleted while other saved definitions, sheets or templates use it; the calculator shows where it is used. History alone does not prevent deletion and retains its saved answers. Recalculating an old formula may require restoring the definition or correcting the formula. An unused definition is deleted without an extra confirmation dialog and can be restored with the definition library’s Undo until you fully quit. Hiding the window keeps Undo available. If a new definition now uses the same name, restoration reports the conflict and does not overwrite the new data.
help.definitions.deleteRule.meaning: Explains deletion blockers, historical independence and session-limited library deletion Undo.
help.definitions.deleteRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 8. Definition deletion Undo is distinct from editor text undo and history deletion Undo. History does not keep a definition undeletable, but semantic identity must not be silently hijacked by an unrelated replacement when recalculating. Exact action access, storage and errors remain design work; do not infer additional blocker categories for unsaved quick input or global draft edits.
help.definitions.deleteRule.location: Delete and restore section of saved-definition management help.

definitions.rename.meaning: Names the command that renames a saved definition and its semantic references.
definitions.rename.context: Editorial command wording for behavior accepted in round 18. Apply the corresponding rename, usage-blocking or session-limited restore rules. This entry does not approve a new permanent editor button or extend text/history Undo. Round 19 places access to definition management in the shared library; accepted definition usage and Undo rules remain unchanged.
definitions.rename.location: Saved-definition actions accessed through the shared library; exact menu/control placement remains interface work.

definitions.delete.meaning: Names the deletion command for a saved constant or function.
definitions.delete.context: Editorial command wording for behavior accepted in round 18. Apply the corresponding rename, usage-blocking or session-limited restore rules. This entry does not approve a new permanent editor button or extend text/history Undo. Round 19 places access to definition management in the shared library; accepted definition usage and Undo rules remain unchanged.
definitions.delete.location: Saved-definition actions accessed through the shared library; exact menu/control placement remains interface work.

definitions.undo.meaning: Names the separate library command that restores a deleted definition.
definitions.undo.context: Editorial command wording for behavior accepted in round 18. Apply the corresponding rename, usage-blocking or session-limited restore rules. This entry does not approve a new permanent editor button or extend text/history Undo. Round 19 places access to definition management in the shared library; accepted definition usage and Undo rules remain unchanged.
definitions.undo.location: Saved-definition actions accessed through the shared library; exact menu/control placement remains interface work.

definitions.inUse.text: {name} is used by other definitions, sheets or templates.
definitions.inUse.meaning: Explains why a saved definition cannot be deleted.
definitions.inUse.context: Show with the actual usage locations when round-18 deletion is blocked. History alone must not trigger this message.
definitions.inUse.location: Diagnostic beside the affected definition or sheet expression; exact visual and accessible presentation remains interface work.

placeholders.name: The saved definition name; preserve its user-provided spelling and case.

definitions.nameConflict.text: The name {name} is already used by a saved definition.
definitions.nameConflict.meaning: Reports a conflict when creating or renaming a global definition.
definitions.nameConflict.context: Round 18 permits one saved definition per case-sensitive global name, with no constant/function collision or overload by argument count. Do not overwrite existing data.
definitions.nameConflict.location: Diagnostic beside the affected definition or sheet expression; exact visual and accessible presentation remains interface work.

placeholders.name: The conflicting global definition name; preserve its spelling and case.

definitions.invalid.text: The definition has errors. Your edits are kept; the working version is unchanged.
definitions.invalid.meaning: Explains rejection of an invalid definition draft without losing editable text.
definitions.invalid.context: For editing an existing definition under round 18. Show the specific syntax, unknown-name, recursion or cycle diagnostic alongside this summary. Kept edits do not imply persisted crash recovery or successful disk storage. For a new invalid definition use its specific diagnostic, not a claim of an existing working version.
definitions.invalid.location: Diagnostic beside the affected definition or sheet expression; exact visual and accessible presentation remains interface work.

definitions.restoreConflict.text: Cannot restore {name}: a new definition uses that name.
definitions.restoreConflict.meaning: Explains why deletion Undo cannot restore without a name conflict.
definitions.restoreConflict.context: Accepted round-18 restore conflict: retain the new definition and do not silently overwrite it. The exact way to resolve the conflict remains interface work.
definitions.restoreConflict.location: Diagnostic beside the affected definition or sheet expression; exact visual and accessible presentation remains interface work.

placeholders.name: The name of the deleted definition being restored; preserve its original spelling and case.

sheet.functionNameConflict.text: {name} is a saved function name and cannot be a sheet variable.
sheet.functionNameConflict.meaning: Reports a sheet-local variable name colliding with a user function.

help.library.rule.text: Press {shortcut} inside the calculator to find sheets, templates and saved definitions in one library, grouped by type. Search by name; definitions can also be found by their descriptions from # comments. Enter opens a sheet, starts a template or opens a definition for editing. Creation and management actions are available here too.
