help.templates.rule.text: Save a copy of a sheet as a template and choose its local parameter variables and default values. Starting the template with parameter values creates an independent named sheet with autosave. Editing that sheet does not change the template. Updating the template is explicit and does not rewrite sheets already created from it. References to saved global constants and functions remain live.
help.templates.rule.meaning: Explains templates as parameterized sources for independent calculation sheets.
help.templates.rule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 2. Do not turn template parameters into global definitions or freeze live global references into numeric snapshots. The launch parameter interface, accepted parameter expressions and error handling are still round-20 proposals; this paragraph does not approve a new launch syntax or a fixed form layout.
help.templates.rule.location: Template creation and reuse section of application help.

help.documents.manageRule.text: Create, rename, duplicate or delete sheets and templates from their management actions. Closing a sheet keeps it saved; a duplicate has its own text. Deleting one document does not require an extra confirmation dialog and can be undone until you fully quit. Hiding the window keeps document deletion Undo available. Other documents, history and definitions are preserved, and restoration does not overwrite newer data. This Undo is separate from text editing and history deletion Undo.
help.documents.manageRule.meaning: Explains document management, close-versus-delete behavior and the lifetime of document deletion Undo.
help.documents.manageRule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 3. Preserve global definition deletion restrictions and its separate Undo. Restoration after a needed global definition has been removed remains a pending round-20 question, not a silently approved cascade or new deletion blocker. Exact action access and naming-conflict presentation remain interface work.
help.documents.manageRule.location: Sheet and template management section of application help.

help.data.exportRule.text: A full export puts sheets, templates, saved definitions and shared settings such as theme, language and copy behavior into one portable file. History is not included and stays on this device. The global invocation shortcut, autostart and window placement also stay device-local. The file preserves calculation references, unit meanings and your own text for transfer between Windows and macOS. No account or cloud synchronization is required.
help.data.exportRule.meaning: Explains the accepted full transfer scope with history explicitly excluded.
help.data.exportRule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 4 with the user correction. The request to remove history was interpreted in the export-scope context; it is not an instruction to erase local records or remove history as a feature. Device-local preferences are excluded from this package. Backup content and application of imported common settings are separate pending decisions. Versioned serialization is required but its format is unchosen.
help.data.exportRule.location: Export section of data-management help, alongside full export.

help.data.selectedExportRule.text: Export selected sheets, templates or definitions together with the saved constants and functions they need, including further dependencies. Unrelated history and other data are not included. Incomplete sheet text can still be transferred; missing definitions are not invented.
help.data.selectedExportRule.meaning: Explains selected transfer with the necessary saved-definition dependency closure.
help.data.selectedExportRule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 5. Include semantic dependencies, not merely text matches; preserve live definition identity and unit semantics. A document may contain incomplete or erroneous expressions without making its container invalid. Do not add unrelated history, account information or device settings to selected packages.
help.data.selectedExportRule.location: Selected export section of data-management help.

help.data.importRule.text: Preview additions and conflicts before importing. Importing the same unchanged object again does not duplicate it. A differing version that conflicts with an existing object is added as a separately named copy by default, with its internal references adjusted together. Existing objects are not overwritten. The file’s structure, version and reference integrity are checked before applying the import as one change. A damaged or unsupported file leaves your data unchanged. An incomplete sheet formula alone does not make the file damaged.
help.data.importRule.meaning: Explains import preview, repeat-import behavior, conflict copies and all-or-nothing application.
help.data.importRule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 6, adjusted to the history-free export in point 4. Object identity and content comparison must preserve distinct objects; same-spelling names are not sufficient identity. Conflicting imported references must point to the intended imported or identical existing definition, not silently capture a different local one. Existing history remains local. Common settings cannot be treated as a second named document; their application policy is pending in round 20. Atomic storage and migration algorithms remain technical work.
help.data.importRule.location: Import section of data-management help, linked from the import preview.

help.data.backupRule.text: The calculator keeps local backups when data change, at most once a day, and also before import. It retains the latest ten copies. Restoring a chosen backup is a separate explicit action with a preview of changes. Ordinary startup does not bring back deleted history. The ten-backup limit does not limit your main calculation history.
help.data.backupRule.meaning: Explains accepted local backup timing, retention and explicit restore access.
help.data.backupRule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 7. Backup composition, including whether it retains history, and replacement-versus-merge restore semantics remain pending in round 20. Do not infer them from the history-free export. Exact daily scheduling, disk failures, integrity checking and recovery are technical work. This describes the future calculator; it does not create a Codex automation or claim an existing backup service.
help.data.backupRule.location: Local backup section of data-management help.
